To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT – Embakasi casuals: Monday pay briefing and stoppage response, 30 November

DRAFT FOR ACHIENG’S REVIEW – NOT YET ISSUED

Brian,

Here is the position for Monday, including what you can say without guessing. The short version is: I made the mess, management apologises, I use the M-Pesa route Njeri has approved, and I do not buy cooperation with another time promise I cannot keep.

1. What actually happened to Friday’s pay

The bank rejected the bulk payment file for all 212 casuals at validation. It did not reject individual payments after processing: nothing in that file was processed.

The immediate cause was the beneficiary-reference column exceeding 20 characters. After the bank’s platform upgrade on 25 November, files have to use its new template. The rejection alert went to the old finance mailbox, so Kevin only saw it after 5pm on Friday, by which time the bank cut-off had passed.

That is the explanation to give. Do not blame the casuals’ records, Ouma, Joseph or the depot. Some phone numbers still need checking, but that is not what caused Friday’s rejection. Finance has accepted responsibility for the missed alert and cut-off, and management owes the men an apology.

Njeri has now approved bypassing the bank file and paying through M-Pesa bulk/B2C. She has also approved:

- KES 500 per person for Monday lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list, in the same M-Pesa batch.
- All M-Pesa charges being borne by the company, not deducted from anyone’s pay or from the KES 500.
- An apology from management, delivered in person at Embakasi on Monday. Since I am travelling, she has asked you to give it.

2. When the money lands

Kevin’s realistic estimate is money on phones on Monday by 11:00. He has specifically said he will not promise earlier.

Keep the qualification “realistic estimate” when speaking to the group. Do not turn it into “guaranteed by 11”, and certainly do not say breakfast time, 6am, before loading or before the trucks leave. If anything changes, give a factual update rather than letting the yard speak for me.

Peninah has checked the telephone list: 198 numbers are confirmed and 14 people could not be reached, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. Those 14 must give Peninah their correct numbers face to face before their payment details can be completed. Do not guess when an individual payment will arrive or assure one of those 14 that he is definitely in the first completed batch. Peninah will confirm each person’s status once his details have been corrected.

Peninah will be at Embakasi from 7:30 with the printed list and her laptop. She can also print payslips for anyone who wants one.

3. What you can promise

You can stand behind these points:

- Management is sorry, and the delay was not the casuals’ fault.
- The approved payment route is M-Pesa, with finance working to the realistic estimate of Monday by 11:00 for properly verified details.
- The KES 500 lunch-and-fare payment is approved for everyone on the affected list.
- Nobody’s M-Pesa charges will be deducted from their money.
- Peninah will be physically present from 7:30 to correct the 14 unreachable numbers and deal with payslips.
- Their grievance has been heard and will be recorded, not brushed aside because there is also an operational problem.
- There will be no dismissal or threat of dismissal on Monday, and no threats about contracts.

What you must not promise:

- An earlier payment time, or an exact minute when money will appear.
- That an unverified number has already been successfully paid.
- Cash advances, additional compensation or any arrangement outside the approvals above.
- That you personally can force an instant M-Pesa reversal or correction if a number is wrong.

Remember Mombasa in 2024: a supervisor said “by lunch”, the money arrived at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. I must never again offer a time simply because it sounds good in the moment. Joseph has also warned that some of these men were previously told “tomorrow” for three days. “I will check and come back to you” is better than another broken assurance.

4. Suggested words to the group

“Good morning. I am sorry. Friday’s payment file was rejected by the bank, and the rejection was picked up after the bank cut-off. That was my failure, not yours. You did the work and expected your pay on Friday. Management apologises.

“We have approval to pay through M-Pesa instead. Finance’s realistic estimate is money on phones by 11 today, for confirmed payment details. I am not going to promise you an earlier time that I cannot control. Everyone on the affected list has also been approved KES 500 for today’s lunch and fare, and the company will meet the M-Pesa charges. Nothing is to be deducted for those charges.

“Peninah will be here from 7:30. Fourteen people still need to confirm their correct numbers with her, and she will also print payslips where needed. Joseph and I will keep you updated. I am asking you to let loading continue while I deal with the pay and each individual’s details.”

Then stop talking and let them respond. Do not read out individual numbers or ask men to display personal payment messages to the whole yard.

5. Monday timings and Ouma

5:30 – You and Joseph at the depot. Get his overnight update and identify any change in the group’s position.

Before the main 6am gathering – Speak to Ouma privately first, away from the crowd. Joseph can be present if that helps. Ouma is loud, but he is under real pressure and should not be treated as a villain. Ask what he is hearing, listen properly, and acknowledge the rent concerns without discussing his private circumstances in front of everyone. Explain the actual payment position, then ask him personally to help keep loading moving while I resolve it.

If anything material changes before I board, WhatsApp me. I am up from 4:30. My flight departs at 7:05, so do not leave an important development until mid-morning and assume I will see it.

6:00 onwards – Address the whole group, apologise and give the approved facts. Joseph should start tracking the Kisumu loading plan immediately. Those trucks must leave by 9:00 or I miss the mill’s offloading slot.

7:30 – Peninah takes the 14 number corrections and payslip requests. Keep that desk orderly and separate from any argument about loading.

8:00 – Hard checkpoint: are the trucks being loaded at a pace that still allows a 9:00 departure? If not, escalate immediately through the joint Ops/HR handling below. Do not wait until 8:45 and then make a desperate payment promise.

By 11:00 – Check actual M-Pesa progress with finance and Peninah. If payments have arrived, acknowledge it and deal with any exceptions individually. If they have not, tell people plainly what is known and when the next update will come.

6. If Ouma’s group refuses to load

First, keep the two issues distinct: the pay grievance is legitimate and is being addressed; under my procedure, a work stoppage is not itself the grievance channel. Do not use that sentence as a threat or as a reason to ignore them.

Any stoppage must be handled by Operations and HR together. You and Joseph handle the operational facts and truck plan; HR must remain involved in the people response. Do not turn it into an Operations-only confrontation, and do not improvise discipline. If you cannot reach me once boarding starts, use the normal HR escalation route and keep a clear update for me.

Speak to Ouma privately again if that will help. Ask what specifically the group is demanding, restate only the approved payment position, and ask them to resume loading while Peninah resolves individual records. Keep the tone calm and public remarks brief. No surrounding Ouma with managers, no shouting across the yard, and no attempt to shame him in front of the others.

Record times, what was said, who was present and any continuing refusal. Operations should assess and escalate the likely effect on the 9:00 departure through the normal operational channel while HR continues handling the grievance. Do not create a made-up payment deadline just to get the trucks moving.

Under the joint procedure, nobody is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. There are to be no contract threats either. The normal grievance route is Joseph first and then HR within 48 hours, but record this grievance now; do not tell angry men to submit a form and wait two days before anyone listens.

You are not walking in there to defend the indefensible. Apologise without flinching, give them the facts I can stand behind, treat Ouma like a man with responsibilities rather than a ringleader, and keep the 9:00 operational deadline visible without turning it into an ultimatum.

Achieng
